report:
## Conclusion

Yes, probiotics can modestly lower blood sugar in type 2 diabetes, though effects are generally small and depend on strain, dose, and duration. Multiple meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials consistently show statistically significant reductions in HbA1c, fasting glucose, and fasting insulin with probiotic supplementation compared to placebo. A meta-analysis of 12 RCTs found significant reductions in HbA1c (SMD −0.38) and fasting insulin (SMD −0.38) (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5491138/). A more recent meta-analysis reported significant HbA1c reduction (MD −0.33) and improved insulin levels (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39114293/), with subgroup analysis suggesting 6–8 week interventions produce the best HbA1c improvements (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11303337/). A broader 2024 systematic review of probiotics and synbiotics across 41 studies similarly supports benefits on fasting glucose, HbA1c, and insulin (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0261561424000803).

However, results are not universal. A 2025 randomized controlled trial found that probiotic supplementation did *not* significantly lower HbA1c compared to placebo in patients with suboptimal glycemic control (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2405457725003109), highlighting variability based on strain type, baseline glycemic control, and trial design. Notably, multi-strain formulations containing Akkermansia muciniphila and related strains (e.g., Pendulum Glucose Control) showed clinically meaningful reductions in A1C and postprandial glucose spikes in a randomized controlled trial (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32675291/), though this trial was funded by the product's manufacturer, warranting cautious interpretation.

**Bottom line:** Evidence from meta-analyses supports probiotics as a modest adjunct therapy for improving glycemic markers in type 2 diabetes, but they should not replace standard treatment, and specific strain and formulation matter significantly.
